newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK security firms booked solid for China takeover.
newsitem.headline: HK security firms booked solid for China takeover.

text.p: You can still get a room and you might be able to get a flight, but if you want to reserve an armoured car or a bodyguard for Hong Kong's handover to China you're probably out of luck.
That's the word from Hong Kong security firms who report a huge surge in demand over the midnight June 30 ceremony and gala festivities.
"If you called me and told me you had a million dollars I still wouldn't be able to help you on the night of the handover," said Bill Thomas, general manager of Jardine Securicor Gurkha Services.

"We are fully committed. Our men will be working all over Hong Kong including in the area of the handover ceremony at the Convention Centre. It is fair to say the handover has generated an enormous amount of business in our line of work."

Hundreds of world leaders are converging on Hong Kong for the ceremony including Chinese President Jiang Zemin, British Prime Minister Tony Blair, U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, British royal heir Prince Charles and former British prime minister Margaret Thatcher.
Public officials will arrive with their own security teams, who will liaise with the Hong Kong police charged with security for the event.
Thousands of private security personnel will also be involved, providing everything from protection as bodyguards to enhanced security around key industrial and utility facilities.
Units of the People's Liberation Army will move across the border from China into Hong Kong when the last members of the British Army have departed soon after midnight.

In addition to the official June 30-July 1 handover ceremony at Hong Kong's Convention Centre, to which 4,000 guests have been invited, there are scores of celebratory concerts, parties and dances scheduled for parks, hotels and function rooms across the city.
Demand for limousines, chauffeurs, gowns and tuxedos on the night of the handover is said by city suppliers to be "unprecedented".
